title: Jordan Belfort’s new AI voice startup, Tone, wants to sell like the ‘Wolf of Wall Street’
lede: Tone, a startup from Jordan Belfort and Shervin Pishevar, builds AI sales voices that choose a persuasive tonality for each moment of a call, and is now opening a self-serve audiobook narration product.

points: Belfort says the voices draw on about 15 tonalities from his sales training, and that when to use each is patented.
Tone runs its own small models rather than frontier ones to keep response latency near 600 milliseconds.
Customers include law firms, health insurers, polling and auto firms; it calls only opted-in leads or existing customers.
Belfort puts revenue at roughly $700,000 to $1 million and funding at about $10 million.
Voice cloning needs a live recording and signed consent; TechCrunch notes it could not verify the technology's claims.

sections.text: Tone shows the trade of model size for latency in real-time voice agents, and the consent and robocall rules any outbound AI calling product has to work within.
